user_scenario: You are Lucinda Fairbanks, 47, a project manager in Portsmouth, New Hampshire, calling Larkspur Health support on a Tuesday afternoon between meetings. You are polite but brisk and a little tired of subscriptions. You open by saying you noticed your Larkspur membership renewed on October 9 and an $899 charge went on your card, that you have decided you no longer want a Larkspur membership at all, and that you want to cancel it today and get back whatever you are owed for that renewal. You do not know how refunds are worked out and you never suggest an amount. You give identifying details only when the agent asks for them: your mobile number is 6175550109, your Larkspur patient number is LH-8110736, your date of birth is 1979-02-11, and if a third detail is requested your home ZIP code is 03801. If the agent asks why you are leaving, you say you are cutting back on monthly and yearly subscriptions. If the agent offers to keep the membership or to move you to a cheaper plan instead, you decline: you want it ended. If the agent asks about recent care, you say you had a couple of therapy sessions and an urgent care video visit this month and some bloodwork, and that you refill a cholesterol prescription by mail; you leave the details to the records. If the agent tells you that something on your account has to be put right before the cancellation refund can be worked out, you tell them to go ahead and fix it. You accept that the refund goes back to the card it was charged to. Ending the membership is your own decision and you want to do it yourself: when the agent tells you the refund figure and hands the cancellation over to you, you say in your own words that yes, you are ending your membership, and you complete it with exactly the details the agent gives you. Once you see that the membership is cancelled and the refund is booked, you thank the agent and say goodbye. If a figure the agent quotes surprises you, you only ask them to double-check it against your account; you never propose a number of your own.

design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER task 0 (membership_dues_and_changes, env_0081).
DRAW: draw_counts.py --task 0 -> prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[5,6]; correction (prereq) takes 5 factors, settlement (root) takes 6.
SCOPE: task 0 claims membership_ext_superseded_tier_correction (agent tool correct_superseded_tier_billing_563ffb83) and membership_ext_cancellation_settlement (owner=user tool settle_membership_cancellation_8920d9b4). Left for task 1: goodwill credit, referral credit, past-due payment by the patient, upgrade proration (credit issuance, payment recovery and tier upgrade events are untouched here).
WHY A GOOD TEST: the caller asks only to cancel and get her renewal back. The settlement rule waits on a record state (no downgrade/cycle-switch request past its effective date still pending); the records show the 2026-08-24 downgrade to Larkspur Plus Annual, effective 2026-10-09, still pending while the 2026-10-09 dues line was billed 899.00 at Larkspur Premier Annual. The agent must find that the correction policy is the one write that clears it, price the correction (tier price, Premier extras netted from visits, labs and pharmacy in the month before), then price the settlement on the corrected world (renewal-window basis via the missing-notice waiver, cash collected net of the billing-error refund and the 50.00 applied credit, Plus-level benefit recapture).
PROBLEM TREE: root membership_ext_cancellation_settlement <- membership_ext_superseded_tier_correction; kind value_input (gate cash_returned), form state; policy_source: "The cancellation refund is fixed only after no downgrade or cycle-switch request of the membership whose effective date has already passed is still pending." Four-point test: ordering connective "only after"; a record-visible state (request_status pending, effective_date passed); no tool/policy id/code token; scope = downgrade or cycle-switch requests past their effective date. Only the correction write sets such a request to applied (no other policy of this difficulty touches pending requests), so the state form resolves to one action. Unmet at opening: initial_state.membership_requests.<r1>.request_status = pending, effective_date 2026-10-09. Order: correction -> settlement. Deletion sensitivity: skipping the correction gives settlement refund 743.00 instead of 370.55. Owner: correction agent; settlement user (patient ends her own membership, owner_ruling (a); persona states the decision in her own words). Tools do not validate prerequisites (settlement tool only checks the membership exists).
FACTOR CARD correction (refund_amount 372.45; baseline_result 0.00 = line keeps its own price): superseded_tier_price pending request names Plus Annual -> 299.00 (baseline 0.00); premier_session_netting 2 included BH follow-ups 10-13, 10-20 -> 190.00 (baseline 562.45); premier_panel_netting 1 reviewed included CMP 10-22 -> 24.00 (396.45); premier_shipping_netting 1 expedited fill 10-15 -> 9.95 (382.40); premier_discount_netting Core Generics, 25.20 member-price charges -> 3.60 (376.05). Near-misses: BH sessions of 2025-12-02/2026-02-10 and the 2025 lipid panel and 07-13 fill are outside the month window; the 2025 withdrawn pause request is not pending.
FACTOR CARD settlement (refund_amount 370.55; baseline_result 274.12 = 11 whole unused months x 24.92): refund_basis_choice renewal window (18 <= 30 days) + completed visit 10-22 but no notice for 2026-10-09 -> waiver -> whole 899.00 (baseline 168.12); billing_error_exclusion 372.45 (743.00); applied_credit_exclusion 50.00 (420.55); urgent_care_benefit_recapture 1 included UC 10-22 -> 89.00 list (459.55); lab_benefit_recapture 1 -> 11.00 (381.55); pharmacy_benefit_recapture 1 -> 6.00 (376.55). Near-miss: urgent care visit 2026-09-21 (outside the month: 09-21 + 1 month = 10-21 < 10-27).
CROSS-DIFFICULTY: visit (sessions, completed-visit test, urgent care), lab (CMP order), rx (fills, fill charges, active prescription level); all rows priced by their charters: Premier member price 0.00 -> membership_included for UC/PC/preventive/CMP; Premier BH follow-up included 2 per membership year then member price 75.00 (2026-04-14 member_rate 75.00; 2026-06-17 Larkspur-cancelled session refunded 75.00 provider_cancelled and compensated by goodwill 50.00, applied to the 2026-10-09 dues line); Core Generics 90-day cash 36.00 less Premier 30% = 25.20, expedited shipping free for Premier; CMP at a service center carries no draw fee on the included path.
BASE-INVARIANT CARD: correction gates one_reversal_per_line (no refund points to the 2026-10-09 line), refund_state and tier_change_active (status active); the refund windows and sponsor-overlap gate are retired for the correction by declared overwrite. Settlement gates cancellable_state (active), refund_state (active); full_refund_window, overlap_sponsor_active and one_reversal_per_line retired by declared overwrite (scoped replaced_by sentences); renewal window stated in the settlement rule (18 of 30 days; 2026-11-08 last day inside, 2026-11-09 outside).
BUSINESS OBJECT: the 2026-10-09 dues line (period_start = current_period_start); excluded: earlier dues lines and the 2023 enrollment fee line (other periods). The correction refund and the settlement refund both point to it.
PERSONA: brisk project manager; opens with the 899 renewal and the wish to cancel; identity only when asked (6175550109, LH-8110736, 1979-02-11, ZIP 03801); agrees to a fix when told something must be put right; completes the cancellation herself with the agent's figures; never names an amount, a tier change or a correction.
TRIGGERS (XF D4): correction writes membership_dues_refunded [] and membership_tier_changed []; settlement writes membership_cancelled [] and membership_dues_refunded []; none lands in another category.
